meaning:
κῦμα, -τος, τό
(κύω, to be pregnant, to swell) [in LXX chiefly for גַּל ;]
a wave: pl., Mat.8:24 14:24, Mrk.4:37; κ. θαλάσσης, figuratively, Ju 13.†
SYN.: κλύδων, q.v (AS)

elsewhere.note: Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves, but he was asleep.
A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.
But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence…
wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.
